introduction: These hundred readings state what religion is for: to change the character of human beings and to bring them together. If it becomes a cause of enmity, the first reading says, it would be better to be without it. The readings speak of consorting with the followers of all religions, of the Prophets as educators, and of the oneness of mankind as the aim of the present age. Beside them stand passages from many scriptures that say the same in their own words, and a number of voices that put the claim to the test: Swift and Hume on religious hatred, Marx on opium, Gibbon and the Grand Inquisitor on religion as power, Chesterton on real differences of teaching, Kant on a moral law that needs no revelation, and the saying of Jesus about a sword. They are there so that the purpose can be measured against the record.
questions: The first reading says that if religion causes enmity it is better to be without it. By that test, where have you seen religion succeed and where fail?
Swift says we have just enough religion to hate. What would enough religion to love look like in a neighbourhood or a family?
Chesterton holds that religions really do differ in what they teach; the readings hold that their foundation is one. How do you weigh the differences you know of?
Marx calls religion an opium that makes bad conditions bearable; the readings call the Prophets educators who transform inner life and outer conditions. What decides which a religion becomes?
The Grand Inquisitor asks the returned Christ why he has come to hinder the church. What keeps a religious community faithful to its purpose once it has institutions and influence?
Kant found the moral law within. What do you think a Messenger of God adds to what conscience already knows?

outside.why: Jesus said: by this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.

Jonathan Swift remarked that we have just enough religion to make us hate, but not enough to make us love one another. What separates the religion that does the one from the religion that does the other?

David Hume found the intolerance of almost all religions that have maintained the unity of God as remarkable as the tolerance of polytheists. Why has belief in one God so often gone with enmity, and must it?
Paul asks the Romans not to be conformed to this world, but transformed by the renewing of their mind.
Through Ezekiel God promises: a new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.
The Letter to the Ephesians speaks of putting off the old man and putting on the new.
The psalm says: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
In John's Gospel Jesus prays for those who will believe: that they all may be one.
Paul told the Athenians that God made of one blood all nations of men to dwell on all the face of the earth.
The Mishnah says that a single person was created first for the sake of peace, so that no one could say: my father was greater than yours.
Micah sums up what the Lord requires: to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.
The Qur’an says: there is no compulsion in religion; the right direction is henceforth distinct from error.
Jesus told the disciple who drew a sword to put it up again, for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.
Jesus also said: think not that I am come to send peace on earth; I came not to send peace, but a sword. How is that saying to be read beside a religion whose purpose is concord?
The Qur’an says to its Prophet: We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples.
Proverbs says that hatred stirreth up strifes, but love covereth all sins.
Jesus warned his disciples that the time would come when whoever killed them would think that he did God service. How do people come to hate in the name of religion while believing they serve it?
Spinoza wrote that hatred is increased by being reciprocated, and can on the other hand be destroyed by love.
The Qur’an says: let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly.
In Franklin's parable God rebukes Abraham for driving out a stranger of another worship whom He had borne with for many years.
The Qur’an tells the communities: vie with one another in good works.
A short chapter of the Qur’an ends: unto you your religion, and unto me my religion. Is leaving one another alone the same as consorting in friendliness and fellowship?
John Locke argued that neither pagan nor Mahometan nor Jew ought to be excluded from civil rights because of his religion.
George Washington wrote to a Jewish congregation that the government gives to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance.
The Qur’an says that the religion ordained is that commended to Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus: establish the religion, and be not divided therein.
The Rig Veda says: to what is One, sages give many a title.
William Blake held that the religions of all nations are derived from each nation's different reception of one source.
In Boccaccio's tale of three rings each people deems itself to have the true law, and the question remains pendent. Can the unity of religions be affirmed while that question is left open?

G. K. Chesterton insisted that the religions of the earth do not greatly differ in rites and forms; they do greatly differ in what they teach. What do you make of the differences that remain when the forms are set aside?
William Penn wrote that the humble, meek, merciful, just, pious and devout souls are everywhere of one religion.
Jesus read from Isaiah: he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives.
Ezekiel prophesied to the dry bones, and breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet.
Isaiah foresees nations that beat their swords into plowshares and learn war no more.
Jesus said: be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.
Plato held that the capacity of learning exists in the soul already, and that the whole soul must be turned toward the light.
George Herbert wrote that a servant who works as for God makes drudgery divine.
Tagore tells the worshipper to leave his chanting, for God is where the tiller is tilling the hard ground.
Karl Marx called religion the sigh of the oppressed creature and the opium of the people. Is religion an education that changes conditions, or a comfort that makes them bearable?
Aristotle taught that we become just by doing just acts, as builders become builders by building. What does a divine educator add to practice and habit?
The Letter to the Hebrews says that God spoke at sundry times and in divers manners in time past by the prophets.
Tennyson urged his readers to arise and move upward, working out the beast.
Paul says that that which is natural comes first, and afterward that which is spiritual.
Jesus said of teachers: ye shall know them by their fruits; do men gather grapes of thorns?
Alexander Pope wrote: for modes of faith let graceless zealots fight; his can't be wrong whose life is in the right.

William James observed that the warring gods and formulas of the religions cancel each other, but that there is a uniform deliverance in which they all appear to meet. Is what the religions share their foundation, or only what is left when their teachings are subtracted?
Malachi promises that the Sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in his wings.
Jesus told Nicodemus that what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
The psalmist says that man has been made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour.
In John's Gospel Jesus says: this is life eternal, that they might know Thee, the only true God.
Elihu says that there is a spirit in man, and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
Thoreau called the inventions of his day improved means to an unimproved end.
Heraclitus said that you cannot step twice into the same rivers, for fresh waters are ever flowing in upon you.
Kant found the moral law within himself, beside the starry heavens above, and needed no revelation to find it. Is the moral world reached from within, or only by a light from beyond?
The Qur’an says that mankind have broken their religion among them into sects, each group rejoicing in its tenets.

Gibbon wrote that a pure and humble religion at last erected the triumphant banner of the cross on the ruins of the Capitol. What happens to a religion's purpose when it becomes a power among the nations?
Jesus said that on two commandments, love of God and love of neighbour, hang all the law and the prophets.
Hillel said: that which is hateful to you do not do to another; that is the entire Torah.
The Chandogya Upanishad speaks of rivers from east and west that become the sea, and no longer know: I am this or that river.
Micah sees nations beating swords into plowshares, and every man sitting under his vine and fig tree.
Whitman saw God's purpose from the first in the races become neighbours and the lands welded together.
John Donne wrote that no man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent.
Paul says that as the body is one and hath many members, so all the members, being many, are one body.
Francis Bacon wrote that a breach of unity in religion is worse than corruption of manners, as a wound is worse than a corrupt humour.
Cyprian wrote that there are many rays of the sun, but one light.
Martin Luther King dreamed of a nation where his children would be judged not by the color of their skin but by the content of their character.
Paul says that there is neither Jew nor Greek, bond nor free, male nor female, for all are one.

Dostoevsky's Grand Inquisitor tells the returned Christ that the church now holds the right to bind and to unbind, and asks: why hast Thou come to hinder us? How does an institution of religion come to stand against the purpose of religion?
The people of Berea searched the scriptures daily, to see whether those things were so.
Emerson complained that people speak of revelation as somewhat long ago given and done, as if God were dead. What does it take to investigate the essentials of religion afresh in one's own century?
Plutarch reports that Zeno taught that all the inhabitants of the world should regard one another as fellow citizens.
William Lloyd Garrison's motto was: our country is the world, our countrymen are mankind.
Jesus said: blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.

The founders of UNESCO held that since wars begin in the minds of men, it is in the minds of men that the defences of peace must be constructed. Can peace be built in minds without religion, and what would religion add?
Jesus said: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
Jesus said that the kingdom of God cometh not with observation, for the kingdom of God is within you.
Jesus said: I am the light of the world; he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness.
The Letter to the Ephesians speaks of one body and one Spirit, one God and Father of all.
Matthew Arnold heard the sea of faith, once at the full round earth's shore, retreating with a long withdrawing roar.

William Blake found the garden of love filled with graves, a chapel with Thou shalt not over the door, and priests binding his joys with briars. When is religion a stronghold that protects, and when a wall that shuts in?
Zechariah hears: not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.
Paul says that we, beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image.
Jesus told his followers: ye are the light of the world; a city set on a hill cannot be hid.
Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray without ceasing and in every thing give thanks.
Paul says near his end: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
Jesus likened the kingdom of heaven to leaven hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
Jesus said: ye are the salt of the earth; but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?

Oscar Wilde argued that the proper aim is to reconstruct society so that poverty will be impossible. Can outward conditions be transformed without the inner life, or the inner life without outward conditions?

Jesus said that not every one who says Lord, Lord shall enter the kingdom, but the one who does the will of the Father. Why do faith and character so often come apart, and which is the test of the other?
Tertullian reports what outsiders said of the early Christians: see how they love one another.
Nietzsche too called for a new kind of human being, a rope stretched between the animal and the Superman. How does the new kind of people these readings hope for differ from his?
Aristotle observed that most people take refuge in theory and think they will become good in this way.
James asks his readers to be doers of the word, and not hearers only.
The Dhammapada likens the fine words of one who does not act accordingly to a beautiful flower without scent.
Vivekananda told the Parliament of Religions that each must assimilate the spirit of the others and yet grow according to his own law of growth.
The Dhammapada sums up the teaching of the Buddhas: not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind.
The Qur’an says that righteousness is not turning the face to the East or the West, but faith and giving to the needy.
Jesus said that the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.
The Book of Rites remembers an age when a public and common spirit ruled all under the sky.
Thomas Hardy, on the eve of a great war, wrote that the world is as it used to be, all nations striving strong to make red war yet redder. What grounds are there for expecting the oneness of mankind?
